meta: Role: Backend Engineer · Level: Junior · Manager: Priya Menon · Buddy: Daniel Wong
scenes.say: Welcome to Northwind Labs, Alex. A quick tour of the Cinema Ticket Management System.

scenes.title: Why we exist
points: Northwind Labs: logistics simple enough for a two-person team
Your project: CTMS — movies, showtimes, bookings, payments
Values: ship small, quality is everyone's job, write it down
say: Founded to prove that a field-service operation does not need enterprise software. Simplicity is the product.
You are joining mid-product: auth, movie catalogue, showtimes, seat booking, and a Stripe webhook are already live.
Three values in practice: merge small PRs, broken tests block everyone, and decisions get a comment in the code.

scenes.title: What you own
points: Platform team — API and data layer
18 Servlets mapped to URLs in the controller package
Services between controller and database; SQL only in DAO
say: As the backend engineer on Platform, you are the last line of defence before the database. Own that boundary.
Each Servlet handles one URL. The mapping is in web dot xml. If a page breaks, start with the Servlet for that path.
Keep SQL out of Servlets and services — it belongs only in the DAO layer, so queries are easy to find and test.

scenes.title: Before you touch anything
points: ISSUE-001: DB credentials hardcoded in source — rotate day one
ISSUE-003: Passwords plain text, no hashing — critical
ISSUE-004: SQL typo at CustomerDAO line 105 — your first fix
say: Anyone with read access to the repo can connect to the database right now. Rotating the credentials is not optional.
Storing passwords without hashing means a single database dump exposes every user account. Treat this as a live incident.
A one-character SQL keyword is misspelled at line one-oh-five. The test you write alongside the fix will be your template for every DAO test after this.

scenes.title: The login request
scenes.point: Login posts to LoginServlet:19, which calls AccountService to check credentials
scenes.say: A login form posts to LoginServlet. Line nineteen reads the username and password, then calls AccountService. At line thirty-two in AccountService, the password is compared with dot-equals — no hashing. That is ISSUE-003.

scenes.title: After login: redirect and filter
scenes.point: LoginServlet:63 redirects by role; AuthFilter:18 guards every protected page
scenes.say: After a successful login, line sixty-three in LoginServlet redirects by role: three is HQ, two is manager, one is staff. Every subsequent request passes through AuthFilter at line eighteen, which checks the session before allowing access.

scenes.title: Database connection
scenes.point: All DAOs get a connection from ConnectionDB:6, where credentials are hardcoded
scenes.say: Every DAO calls ConnectionDB to get a database connection. Lines six and eight contain the hardcoded hostname and password — that is ISSUE-001. Rotating these credentials on day one is your first priority.
